summary: This is a Quarto configuration file that sets up a reveal.js presentation project. It tells Quarto to render all .qmd files and then applies a bunch of styling and behavior settings to make the slides look and function a certain way—like setting the aspect ratio to widescreen, enabling scrollable slides, and adding a background image to the title slide.

explanations.3: The render field tells Quarto which files to process; the wildcard *.qmd means 'all files ending in .qmd in this directory'.
explanations.6: revealjs is the format being configured—it's the library that actually creates the interactive HTML slideshow.
explanations.7: This points to an external CSS file that will add custom styling on top of the default reveal.js styles.
explanations.10: Setting this to false means line numbers won't appear next to code blocks in the slides.
explanations.13: linear mode means you navigate through slides in order, rather than seeing a grid or other navigation interface.
explanations.14: convex is the type of animation transition that plays between slides when you move to the next one.
explanations.18: slide-level: 6 means that heading level 6 (######) in your markdown will be treated as the start of a new slide.
explanations.19: slide-number: c/t displays the current slide number and total slides (like '5/20') on each slide.
